title: GitHub Trending Summary - Daily - 2026-10-30
ranking_basis: Daily GitHub Trending star gains for ranks 1-12; two recent-creation Search discoveries appended as non-comparable supplements.
ranking_explanation: Captured the official daily Trending view at approximately 2026-10-30 17:26 UTC, excluded the list-only jailbreaks repository, and sorted the remaining selected repositories by stars today. TotK Recomp and Mika were found separately with a GitHub Search query for repositories created 2026-10-28 through 2026-10-30 and more than 100 stars; their daily gains are unavailable and they are not ranked against Trending entries.
global_caveat: Trending gains and star totals are point-in-time values and can change after capture. Search supplements are early-momentum discoveries, not part of the daily Trending rank order. No prior-window comparison was collected.

sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Snapshot time: 2026-10-30 17:26 UTC. Scope: daily. Date range: 2026-10-30 through 2026-10-30. Ranking: daily Trending star gains with recent-creation Search supplements appended.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: AI agent infrastructure and user-facing tooling dominate today’s GitHub Trending leaders: Impeccable and DeepTutor each gained more than 2,200 stars in the daily view. Freshly created projects Mika and TotK Recomp add two different signals beyond agent development—on-device mobile automation and native game recompilation.

sections.title: pbakaus/impeccable
sections.description: A command vocabulary for coding agents to steer interface design, critique UX, audit quality, and catch recurring AI slop with deterministic rules.
sections.why_notable: It led the daily star-gain signal; the README describes 24 focused commands and a 62-rule detector that does not require an LLM.

sections.title: HKUDS/DeepTutor
sections.description: A personalized tutoring workspace for learning, explanations, research, and practice.
sections.why_notable: It nearly matched the day’s leader and is the clearest education-focused application in an otherwise developer-tool-heavy list.

sections.title: obra/superpowers
sections.description: An agentic skills framework and software-development methodology for coding agents.
sections.why_notable: A four-digit daily gain on a widely starred project reinforces demand for structured, repeatable agent workflows.

sections.title: Renhuai123/ziwei-doushu
sections.description: An open-source Zi Wei Dou Shu astrology charting engine with calculation algorithms and a knowledge base.
sections.why_notable: It is a distinct non-agent niche among today’s leading gainers, showing that specialized cultural and domain tools can break into the broad daily list.

sections.title: thedotmack/claude-mem
sections.description: Persistent context across agent sessions, compressed and surfaced again when relevant.
sections.why_notable: Its strong gain underscores memory and continuity as a standalone layer in the expanding agent toolchain.

sections.title: pingdotgg/t3code
sections.description: An open agent-harness control surface for managing coding agents from mobile, web, or desktop clients.
sections.why_notable: It makes existing local coding agents remotely accessible across devices and supports several agent providers; its README cautions that the project is early.
sections.unique_caveat: The README says the project is very early and users should expect bugs.

sections.title: milind-soni/OpenMausBot
sections.description: A desktop chat workspace for a team of AI bots, with local-first, bring-your-own-agent operation.
sections.why_notable: It translates multi-agent work into a familiar chat interface, with separate agent identities, models, and connected apps.

sections.title: mattpocock/skills
sections.description: A collection of coding-agent skills packaged for engineers.
sections.why_notable: Its daily gain adds another strong skills-library signal alongside Superpowers and project-specific agent tooling.

sections.title: JetBrains/thinkrail
sections.description: A lightweight IDE built around the pi coding agent and adaptable to a developer’s workflow.
sections.why_notable: It brings the agent-workbench trend into an IDE, rather than treating agents only as chat or command-line tools.

sections.title: CopilotKit/OpenBot
sections.description: A self-hostable AI-coworker template that gives agents a browser, files, and granted tools, with actions decided and recorded.
sections.why_notable: It stands out for controllable, auditable computer access; the maintainers explicitly describe it as an early beta template, not a hosted product.
sections.unique_caveat: The README identifies this as a beta template to clone and self-host, not a hosted product.

sections.title: lightpanda-io/browser
sections.description: A headless browser designed for AI and automation.
sections.why_notable: It is the day’s clearest low-level automation infrastructure signal, distinct from the many application-layer agent repos.

sections.title: anthropics/skills
sections.description: Anthropic’s public repository of reusable agent skills.
sections.why_notable: It adds a major first-party skills library to today’s momentum around reusable agent instructions and workflows.

sections.title: valentderah/totk-pc-recomp
sections.description: A static recompilation project targeting a native Windows build of The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.
sections.why_notable: A GitHub Search result created on 2026-10-29 with strong early star count; it broadens the snapshot beyond AI software.
sections.spoken_name: Tears of the Kingdom PC Recomp
sections.unique_caveat: Early development; README says users need their own legally obtained game files, which are not included.

sections.title: wangzan101/Mika
sections.description: An on-device Android agent that can operate apps and browse the web on a hidden background screen.
sections.why_notable: A GitHub Search result created on 2026-10-29; it brings mobile task automation directly onto the device rather than centering a desktop agent workspace.
sections.unique_caveat: The README labels it a public beta and notes Android-version and device limitations.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content:
- Agent workflow layers: Superpowers, mattpocock/skills, anthropics/skills, and Impeccable package reusable methods, skills, or design commands around existing coding agents.
- Agent memory and control surfaces: claude-mem, T3 Code, OpenMausBot, CopilotKit/OpenBot, and JetBrains/thinkrail focus on continuity, remote control, delegated work, or persistent workspaces rather than introducing a new foundation model.
- Interface quality: Impeccable combines natural-language design commands with a deterministic rule checker; the README says its checks run without an LLM.
- Focused applications: DeepTutor, ziwei-doushu, TotK Recomp, and Mika show strong signals beyond general coding-agent tooling.
- Automation infrastructure: Lightpanda/browser is a lower-level headless-browser project aimed at AI and automation.
- Languages: TypeScript 6/14; Shell 2/14; Python 2/14; Rust, Zig, C, and Kotlin 1/14 each.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The dominant pattern is a growing stack around coding agents: skills and workflows, persistent context, better interfaces, controlled computer access, and remote work surfaces. At the same time, DeepTutor’s daily momentum and the new Mika and TotK Recomp projects show that GitHub’s hottest signals are not limited to coding assistants. The two recent-creation discoveries are useful early-momentum examples, but their star counts should not be compared directly with Trending’s daily gains.

Trending gains come from the matching daily page; supplement star gains are unavailable. No prior-window comparison was collected.
